about: Real historical software defects, reconstructed as minimal deterministic reproducers. Each case is a court: the reference is the FIXED implementation, the buggy candidate carries the historical defect, the clean candidate is a distinct implementation with identical fixed behavior. Domain cases declare an external mutation provider (spec/mutation.md) that reintroduces the defect class for the challenge.

cases.name: Apple Secure Transport 'goto fail'
cases.defect: A duplicated 'goto fail;' skipped the certificate signature verification, accepting any record whose header parsed.

cases.name: bash 'Shellshock'
cases.defect: Importing a function from an environment-style string executed trailing code after the function definition.

cases.name: OpenSSL 'Heartbleed'
cases.defect: The heartbeat responder echoed the declared payload length without checking it against the bytes actually present — reading past the end of the request.

cases.name: Log4j 'Log4Shell'
cases.defect: Nested ${key} lookups expanded recursively without cycle detection — a self-referential configuration recursed instead of being refused.

cases.name: Mars Climate Orbiter unit mismatch
cases.defect: The ground system sent thruster impulse in pound-force-seconds; the flight software consumed the raw value as newton-seconds — the unit mismatch that lost the orbiter.

cases.name: The two-digit-year (Y2K) date bug
cases.defect: Every two-digit year was mapped to 19YY — a 01/01/00 date became 1900-01-01 instead of 2000-01-01.
